title: Ordered sets: comparison, bounds, and quotients

based_on.title: Mathematical foundations: (3) Lattice theory — Part I
A lattice-theoretical fixpoint theorem and its applications

summary: Compare elements in partial orders, distinguish extrema from bounds, and turn a preorder into an ordered set of classes.
abstract: An order describes which elements lie below which others and how whole collections are bounded. A comparison that puts each element below itself and respects chains of comparisons may still place distinct elements below each other. Identifying these elements produces a partial order on their classes. Bounds then let us study maps that preserve comparison. In a complete lattice, every collection has a smallest upper bound and a largest lower bound, and every such map has points it leaves unchanged. These fixed points form a complete lattice too, with their own bounds and a least and greatest member.
